episodes.196897: Showers and embedded thundertorms were moving across SW Nebraska the morning of November 13th, 2024. A severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph occurred at the McCook Airport (KMCK) with this activity.
episodes.197231: A Flash Flood Watch was issued on the second weekend of November, mainly due to a tropical wave moving through the area and a lingering frontal boundary. Saturated soils and moderate to heavy rainfall helped increase the flood and debris flow threat. This tropical wave brought abundant moisture above typical November levels, along with instability, leading to thunderstorms with frequent lightning, strong, gusty winds, and breezy to windy conditions in parts of the islands. From November 9th to 11th, above 3 inches of rain were reported, across SW and N Puerto Rico, but mainly over SE Puerto Rico and Vieques, (with some stations reporting 5 to 6.69 inches in those areas).
episodes.197926: A frontal boundary moved into the region and stalled while Tropical Storm Rafael meandered in the gulf. Moisture from the decaying tropical cyclone streamed north across Louisiana. This produced heavy rain over the area that produced flooding.
episodes.198084: A particularly strong cold front, along with considerable widespread forcing, will bring an unruly spell to the Pacific Northwest. Snow, slides, heavy rain and gusty winds will make conditions hazardous for several days.

events.narrative: A 58 mph wind gust was reported at the McCook Airport via the KMCK ASOS associated with showers and thunderstorms.
KLFY and a local fire department reported multiple streets flooded around Lafayette. Several vehicles were flooded along Ambassador Caffery Parkway. At least one home in Youngsville also flloded.
A stream gage went above flood stage during a heavy rain event in Port Barre. The overflowing ditch flooded a nearby street.
Emergency managers reported flooding on Munoz Rivera St. in Barrio Maldonado, though it remained passable.
A rock/mud slide occurred across hwy 299, between Cedar Flatt and Del Loma. |Lat. 40.80N, Long. 123.38W.
